title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #13

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does fluent reading mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading in a whisper
   B. Skipping words
   C. Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   D. Reading very slowly word by word

2. A word bank is (1 mark)
   A. a type of song
   B. a class list of useful words on one theme
   C. a kind of poem
   D. a place for money

3. What should you do if you make a mistake in your exercise book? (1 mark)
   A. Blame a friend
   B. Tear the page
   C. Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   D. Scribble over it hard

4. What is a good response when you did not understand an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   B. Leave
   C. Do anything
   D. Guess quietly

5. What should listeners do after a group reads aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at the readers
   B. Leave the room
   C. Give kind and helpful feedback
   D. Tear the script

6. What is intonation? (1 mark)
   A. The number of words
   B. The rise and fall of the voice
   C. The size of letters
   D. The spelling of words

7. What does reading with expression mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading in a flat voice
   B. Reading without stopping
   C. Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   D. Reading in whispers

8. Which sentence ends correctly? (1 mark)
   A. The sun is hot:
   B. The sun is hot.
   C. The sun is hot,
   D. The sun is hot?

9. A comma is used to (1 mark)
   A. show a question
   B. begin a sentence
   C. end a story
   D. separate items in a list

10. Why do we listen to oral texts about safety? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To count the words
   C. To sleep
   D. To learn how to stay safe

11. How do you show a question when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Stop reading
   B. Whisper
   C. Read it faster
   D. Raise your voice at the end

12. Which sentence has a verb? (1 mark)
   A. The red bag.
   B. Kamau and his face.
   C. In the morning.
   D. Kamau washed his face.

13. Which is a part of an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. The ending
   B. A page number
   C. A stamp
   D. A price tag

14. What is an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. A story kept secret
   C. A story told aloud
   D. A written test

15. What is the lesson of the hare and tortoise story? (1 mark)
   A. Tortoises are fast
   B. Hares are lazy
   C. Never race
   D. Slow and steady wins the race

16. What does the English proverb Look before you leap teach? (1 mark)
   A. Jump quickly
   B. Think before you act
   C. Look at the floor
   D. Never move

17. What is extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Reading many books widely for pleasure
   B. Reading one word only
   C. Reading only the title
   D. Copying a book

18. In The seller counts the money, what is the predicate? (1 mark)
   A. counts the money
   B. The
   C. money only
   D. The seller

19. Which word shows a choice? (1 mark)
   A. and
   B. so
   C. or
   D. but

20. What should you do while listening to instructions about where to place objects? (1 mark)
   A. Listen to the whole instruction before acting
   B. Look away
   C. Talk
   D. Move immediately

21. What is a mosaic? (1 mark)
   A. A picture made of small pieces
   B. A long story
   C. A heavy load
   D. A kind of song

22. What does rhyme mean? (1 mark)
   A. Words with no vowels
   B. Words with many letters
   C. Words with the same ending sound
   D. Words with capital letters

23. Which of these is a character? (1 mark)
   A. Under the tree
   B. The last page
   C. A girl called Neema
   D. A cloudy afternoon

24. What is leisure time? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeping time
   B. Exam time
   C. Free time when you are not working or in class
   D. Lesson time

25. In the kite passage, what went wrong? (1 mark)
   A. The string broke
   B. The children fell
   C. The wind stopped
   D. The kite flew away forever

26. How should notes be written? (1 mark)
   A. As drawings only
   B. As whole paragraphs
   C. As long sentences
   D. As short phrases of key words

27. Which is the first step in writing a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Sign it
   B. Write the ending only
   C. Choose the theme and characters
   D. Draw the border

28. What is news? (1 mark)
   A. Information about recent events
   B. Old stories only
   C. Songs
   D. Riddles

29. What should you not do with an advert that asks for money from strangers? (1 mark)
   A. Read it carefully
   B. Send money without asking an adult
   C. Check the facts
   D. Ask an adult

30. What should you do first before filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Read all the instructions
   B. Fill any box
   C. Sign
   D. Fold it

31. What is a form? (1 mark)
   A. A page with spaces for information
   B. A story
   C. A kind of song
   D. A picture

32. Which word in The teacher counted the votes is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. votes
   B. counted
   C. the
   D. teacher

33. Which is a polite phrase for asking someone to explain again? (1 mark)
   A. Pardon me, could you explain?
   B. Never mind
   C. Say it again now
   D. You are silly

34. What does a moderator do in a panel discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves
   B. Speaks all the time
   C. Sleeps
   D. Guides the discussion and gives turns

35. What is a choral poem? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A poem performed by a group together
   C. A silent poem
   D. A written test

36. What is repetition in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Changing the title
   B. Repeating words or lines for effect
   C. Adding a picture
   D. Deleting lines

37. What is rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   C. The ink
   D. The page number

38. Which word helps to show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. Green
   B. Yesterday
   C. Table
   D. Finally

39. Which is a poor instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Collect the exercise books and place them on the table
   B. Do the thing with the papers
   C. Wet your hands
   D. Rinse the soap

40. What should you do to check if your instructions are clear? (1 mark)
   A. Ask someone to follow them
   B. Tear them
   C. Hide them
   D. Read them backwards

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three rules for good turn taking. (3 marks)

42. Explain what attentive listening means. (2 marks)

43. Rewrite correctly: we live in nairobi (2 marks)

44. Explain what an instruction chart is. (2 marks)

45. State three benefits of reading widely. (3 marks)

46. Play the role of the soloist in a singing game. Write three short instructions you would sing and say what the group should do for each. (5 marks)

47. Give two rules for looking after class library books. (2 marks)

48. Give three good manners to show when collecting proverbs from an elder. (3 marks)

49. State two uses of a full stop and a capital letter in a sentence. (2 marks)

50. Complete with a preposition: The cat sleeps ______ the bed. (2 marks)

51. Give two adjectives to describe a school bag in an advert. (2 marks)

52. Describe how to mark a line of a poem for reading aloud. (4 marks)

53. Explain how the language train game is played. (4 marks)

54. Explain what a story setting is. (2 marks)

55. Write three instructions for what to do when it starts to rain at school. Use first, then and finally. (4 marks)

56. Give two reasons why neat handwriting matters. (2 marks)

57. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about today's weather. Use at least one comma in a list, two capital letters for names and three full stops. (5 marks)

58. Write a paragraph of four sentences about a time you handled money. Use when at least twice. (5 marks)

59. Describe how a class can collect and keep cultural songs from the community. (4 marks)

60. Describe what a written dialogue shows. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   Fluent readers read smoothly.

2. B — a class list of useful words on one theme
   A vocabulary bank collects words by topic.

3. C — Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   Neat correction keeps the page clean.

4. A — Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   Polite questions help you understand.

5. C — Give kind and helpful feedback
   Feedback helps readers improve.

6. B — The rise and fall of the voice
   Intonation is voice movement.

7. C — Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   Expression shows the feelings in the text.

8. B — The sun is hot.
   A statement ends with a full stop.

9. D — separate items in a list
   Commas separate list items and show short pauses.

10. D — To learn how to stay safe
   Safety texts teach what to do and what to avoid.

11. D — Raise your voice at the end
   Questions often rise at the end.

12. D — Kamau washed his face.
   Washed is the verb.

13. A — The ending
   Stories have openings, characters, events and endings.

14. C — A story told aloud
   Oral narratives are spoken stories.

15. D — Slow and steady wins the race
   The tortoise wins by steady effort.

16. B — Think before you act
   It advises careful thought before doing something.

17. A — Reading many books widely for pleasure
   Extensive reading means reading a lot for enjoyment.

18. A — counts the money
   The predicate tells what the subject does.

19. C — or
   Or offers a choice.

20. A — Listen to the whole instruction before acting
   Full listening avoids mistakes.

21. A — A picture made of small pieces
   A mosaic is made of small pieces of paper or seeds.

22. C — Words with the same ending sound
   Rhyming words sound alike at the end.

23. C — A girl called Neema
   Characters are people or animals.

24. C — Free time when you are not working or in class
   Leisure is free time.

25. A — The string broke
   The string broke and the kite fell.

26. D — As short phrases of key words
   Notes are brief.

27. C — Choose the theme and characters
   Planning comes first.

28. A — Information about recent events
   News reports what has happened.

29. B — Send money without asking an adult
   Never send money to strangers.

30. A — Read all the instructions
   Reading first prevents mistakes.

31. A — A page with spaces for information
   Forms collect information.

32. B — counted
   Counted shows the action.

33. A — Pardon me, could you explain?
   Pardon me and could you are polite.

34. D — Guides the discussion and gives turns
   The moderator keeps order.

35. B — A poem performed by a group together
   Chorus means together.

36. B — Repeating words or lines for effect
   Repetition emphasises an idea.

37. B — The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   Rhythm is the pattern of sounds.

38. D — Finally
   Finally shows the last step.

39. B — Do the thing with the papers
   It is vague.

40. A — Ask someone to follow them
   Testing shows whether they work.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wait for the speaker to finish, keep your turn short, do not always speak first, listen politely.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attentive listening means choosing to give your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker so that you understand and remember what is said.
   Working / marking points: One mark for choosing to pay attention and one mark for understanding or remembering.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: We live in Nairobi.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capital letters and one for the full stop.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: An instruction chart is a poster that shows the steps of a task in order using short words and often pictures.
   Working / marking points: One mark for steps in order and one for a poster or pictures.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary, improves spelling, gives new ideas, makes you a better writer and speaker, gives enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each benefit.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three clear instructions with matching actions, for example Clap two times (the group claps twice), Stir the pot (the group pretends to stir), Turn around (the group turns).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for each matching response, with a total of five marks for three well matched pairs and correct listening steps.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Turn pages gently, never write in them, return them on time, keep them clean (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet politely, listen without interrupting, ask permission to write, say thank you.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: A capital letter begins a sentence and a full stop ends it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct use.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: under (or on, if it sleeps on top)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a preposition and one for a sentence that makes sense.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: strong, big, red, light, new (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each adjective.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Underline words to stress, draw a slash where you will pause, read the line using your marks and check that it sounds natural.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: A pupil starts with a sentence. Each next pupil continues the story with a sentence beginning with when until the story ends.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: The setting is the place and time where the story happens.
   Working / marking points: One mark for place and one for time.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, go into the classroom. Then close the windows. Finally, wait for the rain to stop.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for using all three signal words.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader to understand the message, and it shows respect and builds confidence.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible reason.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example On Monday in Kisumu the sky was cloudy. It was cool, windy and dry. Amina wore a sweater.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence that is complete and correct, one for a comma in a list and one for correct capitals.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two uses of when, for example When I reached the shop, I counted my money. When I paid, I received change. I was happy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear sentence and one mark for correct use of when.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ask elders politely, listen carefully, write or record the song with permission, note the name of the person who shared it and the date, and store it in a class portfolio.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct steps.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people written to show what each speaker says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for showing speakers' words.
